title: Single-serve baked protein oats
summary: Blended oats baked into something between a cake and a bowl of porridge. About 30 g of protein, and it works in an oven, air fryer or microwave.

ingredients.note: The riper the better - this is most of the sweetness.
Optional if your banana is very ripe and your protein powder is flavoured.

steps: Blend the oats, banana, egg, milk, protein powder, baking powder, sweetener, vanilla, cinnamon and salt until smooth. About 30 seconds.
Pour into a greased ramekin or small oven dish. Scatter over the chocolate or berries.
Bake 20-25 minutes until the top is set and springs back, with the very centre still slightly soft.
Let it sit 5 minutes before eating - it firms up as it cools.
tips: Do not overbake it. Protein powder turns dry and squeaky the moment it goes past done - pull it while the middle still looks a touch underdone.
Microwave version: 2 minutes on high in a mug, checking at 90 seconds. Air fryer: 170C for 12-14 minutes.
Bake four in ramekins on Sunday, refrigerate, and microwave for 30 seconds each morning.
Casein or a plant blend makes this moister than whey isolate, which tends to dry out.
health_notes: This is the one to swap the sweetener in. With monk fruit or stevia drops instead of honey it comes to roughly 340 calories and no added sugar at all - the banana carries it.

source.adapted: The standard blended baked-oats formula, with the protein raised and the sugar taken out.
